title: A Classroom Management Strategy For The First Days Of School -of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin recommends splitting the usual start-of-year parent packet into two separate mailings, with a dedicated 'classroom management packet' sent home slightly later to create a memorable behavioral 'shock wave.' The packet should include a friendly introductory letter, the teacher's classroom management plan (which he insists should be teacher-created rather than student-negotiated), a bullying policy, combined homework and restroom policies, and a sample copy of any letter home used as a consequence. He details key implementation steps: thoroughly teach the plan and policies before sending anything home, mail the packet alone rather than mixed with other paperwork, assign reading and discussing it as homework, require a signed return slip, and anchor the back-to-school night presentation around it. Linsin argues that establishing behavioral expectations early, before problems take root, is essential because a classroom that is already out of control is far harder to fix.
points: Split the traditional start-of-year parent mailing into two packets, sending a dedicated classroom management packet slightly later to create impact.
Include a welcoming letter, the teacher-authored management plan, a bullying policy, combined homework/restroom policies, and a sample consequence letter.
Teach the plan and policies thoroughly to students before the packet ever goes home to parents.
Send the packet home alone, assign it as homework to read and discuss with parents, and require a signed return slip.
Build the back-to-school night presentation around the classroom management packet, since classroom management underlies all teaching success.
quotes: The beginning of the school year is the perfect time to send a pleasant behavioral shock wave through your new class of students and their parents.

Some teachers recommend creating a classroom management plan with student input. The reasoning being that if students are involved in making the rules, they’ll have ownership and be more likely to behave. Hogwash.
You’re the authority in the classroom. You set the tone. You make the rules. Therefore your classroom management plan should be prepared and included in this packet.
Detailed modeling and role-play are most effective for teaching your plan, policies, and routines. Again, let students experience the ins and outs of each one before sharing them with parents.
It’s much more difficult to manage a classroom that’s already out of control–like putting toothpaste back in the tube.
The classroom management-only packet is a great way to do this. It gets students and parents on board and on record within the first few days of school.
